## Description

The GST is often called regressive, because lower-income households
spend a larger share of what they earn. But some of what they spend the
most on, such as groceries and rent, is not taxed, and the Canada
Groceries and Essentials Benefit pays lower-income families a benefit
that does not depend on what they buy. In this assignment you will use
the spending records of over 5,000 Canadian households from Statistics
Canada's Survey of Household Spending to work out how much GST
households pay at each level of income. You will measure it against
their income and against their spending, simulate the benefit, and ask
what would happen if the government taxed food and gave the money back
through the benefit instead.

The assignment is designed to give you practice working with survey
microdata in R, and to show how the answer to "who bears a tax?" depends
on how you measure it. It is graded pass or
fail.

**Due: Friday, December 4, 2026 at 9:00pm.**

## Instructions

The questions are in the Quarto document above. Open it in RStudio and
press **Render** before you change anything: it should produce a PDF. If
it does not, fix that first, using the [Introduction to R and
Quarto](/content/introtor.qmd) page.

Then read the description of the data in the document carefully, and
work through the three questions, writing your R code in the chunks
provided and your answers in the text below each question. The hints
under each question point to sections of the [Introduction to R and
Quarto](/content/introtor.qmd) page, which has a worked example of each
step. The sections "Groups of equal size", "Keeping a value from going
below zero" and "Bar graphs" are new since Assignment 1. Each question has a **Comment on the results** prompt,
just above the answer space, that says what your written answer must
cover. Tables must be made with `datasummary_df()`, and graphs must have
readable axis labels. Do not copy and paste, or screenshot, console
output.

## The data

The data are an extract from the public use microdata file of
Statistics Canada's [Survey of Household
Spending](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/62M0004X), 2023.
Each row is one household: 5,485 households in all, with 59 of the
file's 398 variables. The variables keep Statistics Canada's own names
and codes. They cover the household's province, type, size and age, its
income and income taxes, and its spending, split into 52 categories. The Quarto document describes every variable, and says how
to treat each spending category when you calculate the GST.

Source: Adapted from Statistics Canada, Survey of Household Spending,
2023, Public Use Microdata File (catalogue 62M0004X). This does not
constitute an endorsement by Statistics Canada of this product.

## Submission

Submit **the PDF produced by rendering your `.qmd` file** to the
Gradescope assignment called **Assignment 2**, by the due date. When you
upload it, match each question to the page it is on. Only the PDF is
marked, so check that your code, tables, graphs and written answers all
appear in it.

A document that does not render cannot produce a PDF, so render after
every question, not only at the end.

## Marking

The assignment is worth 5% of your final grade, and it is graded **pass
or fail**. A pass earns the full 5%; a fail earns 0.

To pass, your PDF must:

-   be rendered from the assignment's Quarto document, with your R code
    showing;
-   include every table and graph the questions ask for, made from the
    data in R;
-   answer all three **Comment on the results** prompts, covering each
    point they ask about, with reasons that draw on your results and on
    what we covered in class;
-   include your statement on the use of generative AI.

Small mistakes in the numbers do not mean a fail, as long as the work is
complete and the answers engage with the questions. A question left
blank, a missing table or graph, or a written answer that does not
address the prompt does.

## Generative AI

You may use generative AI for this assignment, but you must say how you
used it. The document has a section at the end for this. Failing to
disclose its use is academic misconduct.

## Plagiarism

This is an independent assignment, which I expect you to complete on
your own. It is plagiarism to copy someone else's work verbatim, which
includes R code. Any work you submit should be yours only. However, you
are encouraged to talk to each other to try to figure out how to do the
assignment.
